effect_estimate.comment: Descriptive percentages and frequencies only; no regression coefficients, confidence intervals, or p-values are reported in the chapter.
effect_estimate.value: In the cross-sectional household survey across two low-income settlements in Lahore and Peshawar (N = 80 in Tables 1–2), 52% of respondents had access to safe drinking water, 42% had access to community-level sanitation and waste disposal, 42% had access to restrooms, and 60% experienced post-rain drainage problems (70% in Lahore vs. 50% in KPK). Overall basic urban service access ranged from 62.5% to 87.5% in surveyed Lahore slums versus 22.5% to 65.0% in Peshawar slums. Regarding governance barriers, 70% had never participated in local budget sessions, only 6% rated government departments as satisfactorily prepared to deliver basic services (28% poorly prepared), 57.5% (46) rated politicization of service delivery as high, 41.3% (33/80) rated corruption as high, and local government was rated low on accountability (83.8%, 67/80), responsiveness to marginalized groups (83.8%, 67/80), transparency (81.3%, 65/80), community participation (63.8%, 51/80), equitability of resource distribution (51.3%, 41/80), work efficiency (50.0%, 40/80), and service quality (40.0%, 32/80); satisfaction was 27.5% (22/80; 27% in text) for Provincial Government, 12.5% satisfied and 68.8% somewhat satisfied for Municipal Government, and 7.5% satisfied and 70.0% somewhat satisfied for Local Government. In an illustrative case study (Badar Colony, Lahore, ~3,000 households), an NGO contributing 38% of capital cost and purchasing bulk water from WASA achieved regular water supply and 98% billing compliance over ~8 years.

mechanism_certainty.comment: Cross-sectional descriptive design (capped at <= 2 under CODEBOOK.md §9). Rated 1 because the primary empirical component documents descriptive associations between local governance/devolution deficits and water/sanitation access via respondent survey frequencies without direct primary empirical observation of administrative processing, while institutional mechanisms and case vignettes are drawn from statutory/secondary sources.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines incomplete constitutional/statutory devolution, provincial centralization of water/sewerage in provincial companies, and intergovernmental conflicts (institutional_fragmentation, political_coordination, discretion); informal land subdivision, unserved suburban areas, and regularization/proprietary rights for regulated service supply under the Katchi Abadis Act 1992/2012 (ELIGIBILITY: tenure, property, planning, service_area); citizen budget/NGO co-production participation (participation); and ICT citizen feedback/disciplinary accountability via CFMP (ENFORCEMENT: complaint).
